findings.location: sections/00-opening.tex, lines 66-71 ('... and St Gregory the Great, St Augustine and St Jerome carry it: the garment is charity, the new man put on, Christ himself, shown in the Epistle's plain acts and asked for in the Communion's wish') and lines 79-82 ('St Augustine and St Gregory carry it, with St John Chrysostom's address to those who have partaken of the mysteries: the feast is the Church now, at the Lord's table, ...')
findings.problem: The colon construction gives each reading's composite answer to the Fathers named before it. For the first reading, Gregory (Hom. 38, 9) and Augustine (Sermo 90, 5-6) say the garment is charity. Jerome (In Matth. III, PL 26 cols. 160-161; In Eph. II, col. 508) says it is the Lord's precepts kept, the garment of the new man, and that the new man is Christ. None of the three calls the wedding garment 'Christ himself'; that is Aquinas (Super Matth. c. 22) and, of the Epistle's garment, Schuster. None joins the garment to the Epistle's four acts or to the Communion's wish. research/interpretations.md section 1.3 marks those joins as editorial synthesis, and the reading's own body presents them that way ('Put together, ...'). For the third reading, 'at the Lord's table' is Augustine's phrase. The same reading says Gregory's feast is the banquet of the Word and of Scripture and that he 'does not name the altar at all'. The body attributes every step exactly, so a reader is corrected a few pages later. But the opening's summary implies consensus by proximity (guidance/liturgy/roman-1962-propers.md, 'Evidence and Claim Discipline'), and the concise page 1 and themes are likely to reuse it. This is advisory, not blocking: unlike STU-003, no named witness holds a view contrary to the claim.
findings.required_result: The opening states each reading's answer so that each named witness is credited only with what he says. For example: Gregory and Augustine make the garment charity; Jerome makes it the garment of the new man, woven of the Lord's precepts kept, and names the new man Christ; the reading finds that garment shown in the Epistle's acts and asked for in the Communion's wish. For the third reading, the present-Church feast is credited to Augustine and Gregory, with 'the Lord's Table' given to Augustine or replaced by a term both of them use.

findings.location: (a) sections/40-feast-that-now-is.tex, subsection 'Commanded and asked, healed and held', second paragraph, 'The Postcommunion names the sacrament's work in the language of medicine, medicinalis operatio'; (b) sections/10-each-element.tex, opening paragraph, 'four are the Church's own composition' and 'The Introit's antiphon and the three orations are not Scripture'; (c) psalm citations outside the appointed verses, e.g. Ps 34:3 and 90:15 (sections/05-appointed-texts.tex and 10-each-element.tex), Ps 137:3 (10-each-element.tex) and Ps 138:16 (20-wedding-garment.tex)
findings.problem: (a) The Latin names only 'tua ... medicinalis operatio'. The study's own Postcommunion note (sections/05-appointed-texts.tex) says that 'These thy mysteries' is the 1861 translator's addition. research/scope.md section 1.3 records that the formulary nowhere names the Eucharist; the Eucharistic reading is Schuster's (p. 174), and the next sentence rightly gives it to him. As a textual statement in the study's own voice, the sentence gives the prayer a word it does not contain. (b) The antiphon's source is unidentified. The scope appendix says it 'was not traced to a scriptural or liturgical source'. research/scope.md sections 3.1 and 5.1 record that no Old Latin or Roman psalter was searched, that Schuster suggests the Itala, and that the continuation calls the antiphon a cento of Scripture; neither claim was adopted. Calling it 'the Church's own composition' and 'not Scripture' asserts an origin the evidence leaves open. (c) sections/05-appointed-texts.tex says that 'Psalms are cited in the Missal's numbering, with the Hebrew numbering in parentheses', and guidance/liturgy/roman-1962-propers.md requires the common modern number in parentheses where it differs. The five appointed psalms carry it in the map, loci and dossiers, but Pss 34, 90, 137:3 and 138 are cited without it, so a reader using a modern Bible finds another psalm.
findings.required_result: (a) Say that the Postcommunion names God's work, 'tua ... medicinalis operatio', in the language of medicine, and keep the Eucharistic reading as Schuster's. (b) Describe the antiphon as standing in no verse of the Vulgate, with its source unidentified, and make no claim about its origin; the orations may remain the Church's composition. (c) Give the Hebrew number in parentheses at least at the first citation of each psalm outside the formulary (Ps 34:3 (35:3), Ps 90:15 (91:15), Ps 138:16 (139:16)), or restate the convention so that it is true of the text.

findings.location: sections/90-apparatus.tex, References, 'St Hilary of Poitiers ... Tractatus super Psalmos, in Ps. 118, Aleph 11-12, and in Ps. 140, 3-4', and 'Appendix: Scope and Qualifications', 'Reception' paragraph ('... and with them Rupert of Deutz, William Durandus and Berno of Reichenau, expounded a Mass that shared ... but read another Gospel'); claim at sections/10-each-element.tex, Offertory subsection ('St Augustine and St Hilary read the verse with the Vulgate's past')
findings.problem: guidance/liturgy/roman-1962-propers.md ('References and metadata') requires References to carry exact loci sufficient to verify each claim. The Offertory subsection makes a claim about Hilary's lemma of Ps 137:7. Its evidence is Tract. in Ps. 137, section 15, in the CSEL 22 layer (research/scope.md section 3.7), but References names Hilary's tractates only on Pss 118 and 140. The scope appendix attributes the other Gospel to the Masses of Rupert, Durandus and Berno. research/scope.md sections 2.1 and 3.12 hold that evidence (De divinis officiis XII.19-20; Rationale VI.136; Libellus, PL 142), but neither the clause nor References gives a work or locus for any of the three.
findings.required_result: Add Hilary, Tractatus super Psalmos, in Ps. 137, 15 (CSEL 22, ed. Zingerle, p. 748), to References, or drop Hilary from the sentence. Give the three commentators' works and loci in References, or in the scope clause itself.

findings.location: research/interpretations.md: the table 'The three readings in brief', last column of the feast-that-now-is row; section 3.2, Schuster paragraph ('His standing (Blessed) lets him be one of two carrying authors beside Augustine'); section 4.2, 'Carrying authors' row; section 5, feast-that-now-is row; section 2.3, the introit, collect, epistle and gradual rows (Honorius); section 2.5, 'Alternative' ('Honorius reads the shared chants as the song of a people returning from exile ..., which would make the formulary a homecoming rather than a mission'); section 4.2, 'The Gradual's lifted hands' row ('(Augustine; Honorius)')
findings.problem: After the iteration-1 repairs of STU-001 and STU-003, the study, its comparison table and proper-components.toml name Augustine, Gregory and Chrysostom as the carrying authors of feast-that-now-is. They record Schuster's own reading of this Gospel's banquet as the heavenly one (The Sacramentary III, p. 173; research/scope.md section 3.6) beside the claim, and they cite Honorius only in the element-by-element section. The canonical interpretation record still names Schuster a carrying author and does not set his p. 173 reading beside the controlling claim in section 3.1. It still keeps Honorius in the call-to-the-nations reading, and section 2.5 still credits him with an implication about 'the formulary', the attribution STU-001 removed from the study. The concise components (concise-overview, concise-themes, concise-commentary) and both homily components declare research/interpretations.md as a reference, so their authors will read the superseded statements. research/production-review.md reports the divergence as an upstream research item. It is advisory because the reviewed study and manifest are correct, and the record discloses the divergence.
findings.required_result: At the next research revision of this leaf, research/interpretations.md agrees with the reviewed study. Augustine, Gregory and Chrysostom are the carrying authors of feast-that-now-is. Schuster is a supporting witness for the Gradual, Secret and Postcommunion, with his p. 173 heavenly-banquet reading recorded beside the controlling claim. Honorius is removed from the call-to-the-nations rows and alternative, and no sentence credits him with a reading of the formulary; his shared-element readings stay in research/scope.md section 3.12.

observations.note: This one sentence form in the opening has now produced a blocking finding (STU-003, iteration 0) and an advisory (STU-008). guidance/liturgy/propers-three-documents.md says how a reading's carrying authors are chosen and recorded, but not how an opening or concise overview may name them beside the reading's thesis without implying that they hold all of it. summary: Cold review of the expansive study main.tex for liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/59-nineteenth-after-pentecost (build hash 58968423...a85657, 33 physical pages, inside 20-50; every sealed input hash matched REVIEW_INPUTS). Checked evidence: the Latin against propers/verified.md; the Douay verses in the Challoner verse-text artifacts; every English patristic quotation at its locus in the tracked NPNF1-6, NPNF1-8, NPNF1-10, NPNF1-13 and ANF 1 texts; Gregory Hom. 38 in the tracked Wikisource Latin (including the claim that the homily names neither Israel nor the nations); Hilary In Matth. 22 and Tract. in Pss 118 and 140 in the PL 9 layer; Jerome on Mt 22 and Eph 4 in the IA OCR of the registered PL 26 scan; Aquinas on Eph 4 in the 1857 OCR; Augustine on Ps 104 in the Wikisource Latin; Bellarmine, Schuster (quotations and page numbers) and the 1883 Liturgical Year; the chronology rows against composition.yaml and the generated annotations; and the occurrence rubrics against research/context.md. Every quotation checked was exact. The three readings are distinct, each carries all ten elements and its own four senses, and each is carried by three Fathers with developed contributions; the prior blocking findings STU-001 (Honorius), STU-002 (Gospel and Epistle dossiers) and STU-003 (Schuster) are repaired, and the standing advisories STU-004 to STU-007 are cleared. Limits: PG 27 and PG 55 Greek, the PL 26 page images and Honorius and Sicard were not re-read, and word counts were not recomputed. Verdict PASS with five advisories: STU-008 to STU-010 are on the study and STU-011 and STU-012 on research records.
